courses.title: Lesson 1 — A Day with a Phone
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary → Grammar → Comprehension → Speaking → Writing
courses.new: present simple, time expressions (at six o'clock, every morning, in the evening), and the five core TOEFL question types
howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order, one part at a time. Play the MP3 of a part before you open its sheet.
Record your speaking answers on your phone, and send them with your writing and your self-report.
Open part 10, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 09 are finished.

howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order. Part 04 is grammar and has no audio; part 05 needs its audio, because the three sounds of *-ed* cannot be heard from the page.
Record your speaking answers on your phone, and send them with your writing and your self-report.
Open part 11, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 10 are finished.

courses.title: Lesson 5 — The Two O'Clock Class
courses.topic: Teaching computers, volunteering and small steady progress
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary → Grammar → Comprehension → Speaking → Writing
courses.new: the present perfect continuous with for and since, the -ing ending and the weak been, a longer passage of 481 words, and the last new question type: the writer's attitude. The comprehension set reaches ten questions, the size of a real TOEFL set.
howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order. Part 04 is grammar and has no audio; part 05 needs its audio most of all, because *has*, *been* and *-ing* all shrink in speech.
Part 06 has ten questions this time. Do it in one sitting, with a clock, the way the exam will be.
Open part 11, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 10 are finished.

courses.title: Lesson 6 — A Plan for Tuesday
courses.topic: Planning a week of study around the hours of electricity
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary → Grammar → Comprehension → Speaking → Writing
courses.new: the future with will and going to, the short 'll and the weak going to, and the present perfect against an exact date. The passage holds at about 500 words: from here the text gets harder rather than longer, and the question set does not change at all.
howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order. Part 04 is grammar and has no audio; part 05 needs its audio most of all, because *will* shrinks to a single consonant and *going to* becomes one word.
Part 06 is the same ten questions, in the same eight types, as Lesson 5. Nothing in the format is new — only the text. Do it in one sitting, with a clock.
Open part 11, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 10 are finished. The five games come days later, not the same evening.

courses.title: Lesson 7 — The Bench by the Stairs
courses.topic: A student repair bench: rules, faults and judgement
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary → Grammar → Comprehension → Speaking → Writing
courses.new: the modals can, could, should, must and have to, the weak can against can't and have to said as hafta, and the state verbs that never take the continuous. The passage stays at about 500 words; the question set is unchanged.
howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order. Part 04 is grammar and has no audio; part 05 needs its audio most of all, because *can* and *can't* are told apart by a vowel, not by the *t*.
Section 3.5 of the grammar sheet is the one to read twice: *must not* and *do not have to* are opposites, and the passage uses both within four lines of each other.
Open part 11, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 10 are finished. The five games come days later, not the same evening.

courses.title: Lesson 8 — The Line We Share
courses.topic: A shared connection, a class at eight, and an application abroad
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary → Grammar → Comprehension → Speaking → Writing
courses.new: the first and second conditional, the contracted 'd for would and had, the weak if-clause, and the present simple in time clauses. The passage stays at about 500 words for the third lesson running, and the question set is unchanged.
howToWork: Play **01-passage.mp3** and listen twice with no text in front of you. Do not open the PDF yet.
Then work through the parts in number order. Part 04 is grammar and has no audio; part 05 needs its audio most of all, because *would* and *had* arrive as the same single sound.

Read the **Come back to** section before the conditionals, not after. The rule about *when* and *until* is the same rule the *if*-clause follows, and the conditionals are far easier once it is in place.
Open part 11, the answer key, only when parts 01 to 10 are finished. The five games come days later, not the same evening.

courses.title: Progress Test 1 — after Lessons 1 to 3
courses.topic: Everything so far: daily routine, keeping files safe, and computing
courses.time: about 90 minutes, in one sitting if possible
courses.skills: Listening → Reading → Vocabulary and grammar → Writing → Speaking
courses.new: two texts she has never seen, the eight TOEFL question types from Lessons 1 to 3, and a score that says which lesson to go back to
howToWork: Sit the whole test in one go if you can, with a clock, and do not open part 06 until you have finished.
Start with **01-listening.mp3** and do not read the sheet before you play it. Sections 2, 3 and 4 are paper only.
Play **05-speaking.mp3** last and record your three answers.
Then open part 06, mark yourself out of 100, and read the table that says which lesson to go back to.
